               adopted provisions of said act shall be deemed a violation of this chapter and be
               subject to penalties as herein provided.

This chapter shall take effect May 1, 2004.

               definitions set forth in the Illinois Liquor Control Act and below: Alcohol means the product of distillation of any fermented liquid, whether rectified or diluted,

               not include denatured alcohol or wood alcohol. Alcoholic liquor means alcohol, spirits, wine and beer, and every liquid or solid, patented or not,

questions.prompt: Which of these is not allowed in a residential neighborhood in Arlington Heights?
choices: Keeping up to four cats or dogs over four months old
Raising chickens, ducks, geese, pigs, or horses
Walking a dog on an eight-foot leash
Owning a pet that has been spayed or neutered
questions.answer: Raising chickens, ducks, geese, pigs, or horses
questions.excerpt:
The purpose of this Chapter is: a. To provide security of persons against annoyance, intimidation or injury by animals. b. To prevent nuisances by animals through responsible ownership. c. To protect animals from abuse and neglect.

Unless otherwise expressly stated, the following words or terms shall, for the purpose
               of this Chapter, have the meanings indicted in this Section: Animals. Any creature other than a human being. Bite. Any activity with the mouth of an animal which breaks through the skin, but
               does not necessarily have to draw blood. Cruelty to Animals. Any one of the following activities: 1. To overwork, overdrive, beat, torture, torment, poison, mutilate or inhumanely kill
                  any animal; 2. To unnecessarily fail to provide any animal with proper food, drink, shelter or air; 3. To abandon or fail to reclaim any impounded animal; or 4. To inhumanely treat any animal in any manner. Dangerous Animal. Any animal which is inherently incapable of being domesticated and
               is considered by the law to be inherently dangerous (ferae naturae). Diseased Animal. Any animal infected with a contagious or infectious disease, including
               those diseases contagious or infectious only to animals. Leash. A strong cord, thong or chain, not more than eight feet in length. Neutered. Any animal that has been spayed or castrated. Owner. Any person having a right of property in an animal, or who keeps or harbors
               an animal, or who has it in his or her care, or acts as its custodian, or who knowingly
               permits an animal to remain on or about any premises occupied by him or her. Person. Any natural person, partnership, trust, corporation or association. Whenever
               used with respect to any penalty, the term person, as applied to partnerships or associations,
               shall mean the partners or members thereof, and as applied to trusts or corporations,
              …

choices: You may bury it in your yard within 24 hours

questions.prompt: Besides one member from the architectural review commission, how many other people serve on Barrington's plan commission?
questions.answer: Seven
questions.excerpt:
There is hereby created a plan commission for the village which shall consist of a
               member of the architectural review commission who shall be an ex officio member, and
               seven additional members who shall be appointed by the president, subject to confirmation
               by the board of trustees. (1973 Code § 16-1; amd. 2003 Code)

Each appointed member of the plan commission shall serve for a term of three years
               expiring on December 31, or until his successor is appointed and qualifies, but terms
               shall be staggered in order that at least two members shall be appointed or reappointed
               each year. An appointment to fill a vacancy shall be for the unexpired portion of
               the term. (1973 Code § 16-3)

A. Chairman and vice chairman. The president shall designate one member as the chairman of the plan commission and
               one member as the vice chairman to serve as chairman in the absence of the chairman. B. Meetings. 1. The plan commission shall meet at such time as it may determine. 2. Special meetings may be called by the chairman or by any two members of the commission. 3. Meetings shall be in compliance with the state open meetings act 1 . C. Quorum; vote requiremen. A majority of the plan commission shall constitute a quorum, but no final action
               shall be taken on any measure before it except with the concurrence of four members.
               The chairman shall vote with the other members of the commission. D. Rules. The plan commission may adopt rules regulating the procedure of all meetings of the
               plan commission. Such rules shall be filed in the office of the village clerk and
               may be amended at any meeting, such rules to be effective upon filing in the office
               of the clerk. (1973 Code §§ 16-5, 16-6, 16-8; Ord. 96-2614, 8-26-1996; amd. 2003 Code) State Law reference— 1 5 ILCS 120/1 et seq.

There is hereby created a plan commission for the village which shall consist of a

               seven additional members who shall be appointed by the president, subject to confirmation
               by the board of trustees. (1973 Code § 16-1; amd. 2003 Code)

Each appointed member of the plan commission shall serve for a term of three years
               expiring on December 31, or until his successor is appointed and qualifies, but terms
               shall be staggered in order that at least two members shall be appointed or reappointed
               each year. An appointment to fill a vacancy shall be for the unexpired portion of
               the term. (1973 Code § 16-3)

A. Chairman and vice chairman. The president shall designate one member as the chairman of the plan commission and
               one member as the vice chairman to serve as chairman in the absence of the chairman. B. Meetings. 1. The plan commission shall meet at such time as it may determine. 2. Special meetings may be called by the chairman or by any two members of the commission. 3. Meetings shall be in compliance with the state open meetings act 1 . C. Quorum; vote requiremen. A majority of the plan commission shall constitute a quorum, but no final action
               shall be taken on any measure before it except with the concurrence of four members.

A. Purpose. The purpose of this chapter is to establish policies and procedures for constructing
               facilities on rights-of-way within the village's jurisdiction, which will provide
               public benefit consistent with the preservation of the integrity, safe usage, and
               visual qualities of the public rights-of-way and the village as a whole. B. Intent. In enacting this chapter, the village intends to exercise its authority over
               the rights-of-way in the village and, in particular, the use of the public ways and
               property by utilities, by establishing uniform standards to address issues presented
               by utility facilities, including without limitation: 1. Prevent interference with the use of streets, sidewalks, alleys, parkways and other
               public ways and places; 2. Prevent the creation of visual and physical obstructions and other conditions that
               are hazardous to vehicular and pedestrian traffic; 3. Prevent interference with the facilities and operations of the village's utilities
               and of other utilities lawfully located in rights-of-way or public property; 4. Protect against environmental damage, including damage to trees, from the installation
               of utility facilities; 5. Protect against increased stormwater run-off due to structures and materials that
               increase impermeable surfaces; 6. Preserve the character of the neighborhoods in which facilities are installed; 7. Preserve open space, particularly the tree-lined parkways that characterize the village's
               residential neighborhoods; 8. Prevent visual blight from the proliferation of facilities in the rights-of-way; and 9. Assure the continued safe use and enjoyment of private properties adjacent to utility

The DuPage Airport Authority may establish tow-away zones in which the parking of
            vehicles is prohibited or restricted. The location of such zones and the prohibition
            or restriction shall be clearly designated by signs posted or other conspicuous markings,
            and such signs or markings shall indicate that vehicles in violation will be towed
            and impounded.

The term "tow-away zone" shall mean an area designated by the Board of Commissioners
               of the DuPage Airport Authority (hereinafter the "Board of Commissioners") where vehicles
               may be impounded upon violation of this Chapter. A current list of such zones appears
               at Appendix 13-A.

The term "impounded" shall mean the removal of the vehicle to a storage facility either
               by a law enforcement officer or authorized agent of the DuPage Airport Authority or
               by a contractor for towing and storage in response to a request from a law enforcement
               officer or authorized agent of the DuPage Airport Authority.

Where signs are erected or other markings exist giving notice thereof, no person shall
            park or leave standing or unattended a motor vehicle where prohibited or restricted
            by such signs or other markings. Violators of this Chapter may be assessed a fine up to $25 per day, not to exceed
            $500. Each calendar day that such violation continues shall constitute a separate
            offense. A vehicle in violation of this Chapter may be impounded, with or without citation
            and without giving prior notice to its owner, when the vehicle is illegally parked
            in a tow-away zone as established by this Chapter.

questions.prompt: Does East Peoria's comprehensive plan by itself control how you use your private property?
choices: Yes, it has the force of law on every lot
No, it is only advisory and cannot control the use of private property
Yes, and it also forces the city to spend money on every idea
Only if your lot is downtown
questions.answer: No, it is only advisory and cannot control the use of private property
questions.excerpt:
It is the purpose of this chapter to adopt preliminary reports, maps and drawings,
               with amendments thereto, in connection with the preparation of a comprehensive plan
               consisting of a written statement of goals and policies, maps and other drawings,
               and written material describing present and proposed future development of the city
               contiguous unincorporated area. The plan is advisory and according to law cannot regulate
               or control the use of private property in any way or cannot commit the city or any
               other public agency to the expenditure of public funds. The comprehensive plan or
               parts thereof may be implemented only when its proposals are incorporated in the official
               map, zoning, subdivision and other regulations and improvement projects duly enacted
               by the city council or other public agency. (Code 1994, § 5-1-2)

Previously printed maps, drawings and other descriptive material attached hereto and
               incorporated herein by reference and made a part of this chapter shall be identified

               of the Preliminary Comprehensive Plan Ordinance, passed on September 3, 1968, by the
               City Council of the East Peoria, Illinois, approved by James C. Spinder, Mayor, Attest
               Robert L. Arnold, City Clerk." (Code 1994, § 5-1-3)

questions.prompt: In Edwardsville, may you drink beer, wine, or other alcoholic liquor on a public sidewalk, street, or alley?
choices: Yes, if you stay out of the roadway
Yes if the drink is in a plastic cup
questions.answer: No
questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- State Law reference— Liquor Control Act of 1934, 235 ILCS 5/1-1 et seq.

As used in this chapter, the term "alcoholic liquor" includes alcohol, spirits, wine,
               beer and every liquid or solid, patented or not, containing alcohol, spirits, wine
               or beer and capable of being consumed as a beverage by a human being, except for any
               such liquid or solid containing 0.5 percent, or less, of alcohol by volume. (Code 1978, § 610.01; Ord. No. 1551-9-74, 9-3-1974)

Any person, firm or corporation who violates the provisions of this chapter shall
               be fined as provided in section 1-10 . (Code 1978, § 610.99; Ord. No. 5308-4-01, 4-17-2001)

No person shall drink or consume alcoholic liquor on the streets, public walkways,
               highways, alleys or thoroughfares within the city limits. (Code 1978, § 610.02; Ord. No. 1551-9-74, 9-3-1974)

No person shall drink or consume alcoholic liquor upon any private premises commonly
               used for public parking and driveway purposes in the city without first having obtained
               permission to do so from the owners thereof. (Code 1978, § 610.03; Ord. No. 1551-9-74, 9-3-1974)

No pedestrian shall transport alcoholic liquor in unsealed containers on the streets,
               public walkways, highways, alleys or thoroughfares, or upon or across any private
               premises commonly used for public parking and driveway purposes in the city without
               first having obtained permission to do so from the owners thereof. (Code 1978, § 610.04; Ord. No. 1551-9-74, 9-3-1974)

(a) It is found, determined and declared as follows: (1) The cost of the extension of the district's existing sanitary interceptor sewer system
               and the construction of necessary appurtenant infrastructure improvements, such as
               pumping stations, to unsewered areas must be partially or totally borne by those persons,
               corporations, developers, or others benefitting from such improvements, including
               but not limited to, newly annexed areas. (2) That it will conduce to the public health, comfort or convenience of the public if
               a reasonable infrastructure participation fee is established. (3) In order to make cost of the extensions of such sanitary interceptor sewers and construction
               of infrastructure improvements equitable to those receiving the benefits thereof,
               and in order to provide part of the cost for such construction, a fee is established. (b) There is hereby established an infrastructure participation fee which shall be determined

               the area is annexed or an agreement is approved. The balance of the infrastructure
               participation fee, depending upon the service area, shall be payable prior to signing
               of the state environmental protection agency per application for on-site sanitary
               sewer improvements or as determined by the board. (c) The service areas and the amounts payable in each service area, inclusive of the $1,400.00

This Zoning Code is adopted with the purpose of protecting and promoting the public
               health, safety, morals, comfort and general welfare. The fulfillment of this purpose
               is to be accomplished by seeking: (A) To establish adequate standards for the provision of light, air and open spaces. (B) To zone all properties with a view to conserving the value of buildings and land and
                  encouraging the most appropriate use of land throughout the Village. (C) To lesson congestion on the public streets, and to facilitate the provision of adequate
                  transportation, and of other public requirements and services such as water, sewerage,
                  schools and parks. (D) To avoid hazards to persons and damage to property from inappropriate development
                  of lands and provide for adequate drainage, curbing of erosion and reduction of flood
                  damage. (E) To avoid undue concentration of population and to prevent the overcrowding of land,
                  thereby ensuring proper living and working conditions and preventing the development
                  of blight and slums. (F) To foster a more rational pattern of relationship between residential, business, commercial
                  and industrial uses for the mutual benefit of all. (G) To provide for and preserve appropriate open space. (H) To protect residential, business, commercial and industrial areas alike from harmful
                  encroachment by incompatible uses, and to ensure that land allocated to a class of

questions.prompt: Before digging a hole or making a tunnel under a public street, sidewalk, alley, or parkway in Harwood Heights, you must first:
choices: Get a permit from the village clerk
Get a note from nearby neighbors
Fill it the same day so no permit is needed
questions.answer: Get a permit from the village clerk
questions.excerpt:
Chapters:

Sections:

A. It is unlawful to make any opening or excavation in or tunnel under any public street,
               alley, sidewalk, parkway or other public place in the village, without having first
               secured a permit therefor. Applications for such permits shall be made to the village
               clerk, and shall specify the intended location and purpose of such opening, excavation
               or tunnel. B. In each case the applicant shall agree to pay all of the cost of restoring such streets,
               alley, sidewalk, parkway or other public place and the surface thereof to the condition
               that existed before the opening, excavation or tunnel was made. (Prior code § 96.15)

A. No permit required in this chapter shall be issued until the applicant has deposited
               with the village clerk a cash bond in the amount set forth in the village fee schedule
               appended to this code as Appendix 1. Such deposit shall be used if the applicant's
               restoration of such street, alley, sidewalk, parkway or other public place and the
               surface thereof to the condition that existed before the opening, excavation or tunnel
               was made is not completed to the satisfaction of the village of Harwood Heights; provided,
               that the applicant shall in each case, do all necessary backfilling or cause the same
               to be done. In restoring such street, alley, sidewalk, parkway or other public place,
               the village may use its own employees and equipment and make reasonable charges therefor,
               or it may engage the services of other persons and equipment and charge the cost thereof
               to the applicant. Any balance of the cash bond deposit remaining after the deduction
               of such charges or costs shall be returned to the applicant and any charges over the
               cash bond deposit shall be collected from…

               shall: (1) Superintend the opening, grading, paving, construction and repairing of all streets,

                  meeting of the council of each municipal year, submit a detailed statement as to such
                  tools, implements and property and their condition. (Code 1964, §§ 12.01(b) (e), 12.02(d); Code 1974, § 16-2)

               and upon delivery of his records and property as provided in section 2-100 , the superintendent shall be given a receipt therefor in duplicate from his successor,

questions.prompt: When do Lombard's bicycle rules start applying to a bike that has training wheels?
choices: As soon as the wheels are 20 inches or larger
After the training wheels have been taken off
Whenever a child is riding it
questions.answer: After the training wheels have been taken off
questions.excerpt:
For the purpose of this chapter, a bicycle is defined as any vehicle consisting of
               an arrangement or combination of two wheels, 20 inches or more in diameter, one following
               the other or a vehicle commonly known as tricycle, but for the purposes of this ordinance
               included under the name 'bicycle,' consisting of three wheels 20 inches or more in
               diameter with two wheels following one wheel, supported by a frame, propelled wholly
               or in part by the feet acting upon pedals. (The temporary attachment of training wheels
               excludes the vehicle from the provisions of this chapter until such training wheels
               have been removed).

(A) It is unlawful for any person to do any act forbidden or fail to perform any act required
               in this article. (B) The parent of any child under 16 years of age and the guardian of any ward under 16
               years of age shall not authorize or knowingly permit that child or ward to violate
               any of the provisions of this ordinance, and any parent or guardian of a child under
               16 years of age authorizing or knowingly permitting such violation shall, upon conviction
               thereof, be guilty of a misdemeanor and shall be punished by imposition of the penalties
               provided for by this ordinance. (C) The regulations applicable to bicycles shall apply whenever a bicycle is operated
               upon any highway or upon any path set aside for the use of bicycles subject to those
               exceptions stated herein.

Every person riding a bicycle upon a roadway shall be granted all the rights and shall
               be subject to all of the duties applicable to the driver of a vehicle under the Lombard
               Traffic Code, except where this Chapter otherwise provides and except where provisions
               of that code by their nature have no application.

questions.answer: 48 hours
questions.excerpt:
The following words and phrases, when used in this title, shall, for the purpose of
               this title, have the meanings respectively ascribed to them in this chapter. (Prior code § 11-101 (part).)

Authorized emergency vehicle means vehicles of the fire district, police vehicles, ambulances, and other emergency
               vehicles as are or shall be designated or authorized by the village board. (Prior code § 11-101(part).)

Business district means the territory contiguous to and including a street when 50 percent or more
               of the frontage thereon for a distance of 300 feet or more is occupied by buildings
               used for public purposes. (Prior code § 11-101(part).)

Driver means every person who operates or is in actual physical control of a vehicle. (Prior code § 11-101(part).)

Motor vehicle means every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rail. (Prior code § 11-101(part).)

Park means the standing of a vehicle, whether occupied or not, otherwise than temporarily
               for the purpose of and while actually engaged in loading or unloading. (Prior code § 11-101 (part).)

Pedestrian means any person afoot. (Prior code § 11-101 (part).)

Person means every natural person, firm, association, copartnership or corporation. (Prior code § 11-101(part).)

Police officer means every officer of the municipal police department or any officer authorized
               to direct or regulate traffic or to make arrests for violations of traffic regulations. (Prior code § 11-101(part).)

Private road or driveway means every way or place in private ownership and used for vehicular travel by the
               owner, but not by other persons unless they have express or implied permission from
               the owner. (Prior code § 11-101(part).)

Right-of-way means the privilege of the immediate use of the roadway. (Prior code § 11-101(part).)

Roadway means that part of a street ordinarily used for vehicular travel.…

questions.excerpt:
A. Adoption by reference. Pursuant to the authority of 625 ILCS 5/20-204 of the Illinois vehicle code, the
               Illinois vehicle code, 625 ILCS 5/1-100 et seq., is hereby adopted by reference as
               if fully set forth herein. B. Citations for traffic violations. Citations for violations of state traffic laws adopted by subsection A of this section
               shall refer to the Illinois vehicle code section number of the law violated, but the

               violations of any other provisions of this title shall refer to the number of the

               vehicle code (except 625 ILCS 5/11-501 "driving while under the influence of alcohol,

questions.prompt: What is this set of village rules officially called?
questions.answer: Village Liquor Code
questions.excerpt:
This chapter shall be known and may be cited as the Village Liquor Code. (Ord. No. 2013-06-18-02, § 1(1-1), 6-18-2013)

It is hereby declared to be the intent and purpose of the village board in adopting
               and administering the provisions of this chapter: (1) To declare that the control of the availability of alcoholic liquor to the public
                  in general, and to minors in particular, promotes the public health, safety and welfare; (2) To encourage responsibility in the consumption of alcoholic liquor by sound and careful
                  control and regulation of the sale and distribution thereof; (3) To recognize that the abuse of alcoholic liquor is a significant social problem that
                  requires the utilization of public resources to educate citizens, to rehabilitate
                  habitual users and to creatively enforce laws and ordinances; and (4) To ensure that the number of retail outlets, and the manner in which they are operated,
                  is such that they can be adequately policed by local law enforcement agencies, so
                  that the abuse of alcohol and the occurrence of alcohol-related crimes and offenses
                  is kept to a minimum. (Ord. No. 2013-06-18-02, § 1(1-2), 6-18-2013)

The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the
               meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates
               a different meaning: Agent means every officer, associate, member, representative, manager, partner, director,
               shareholder, employee or other person acting with the knowledge of, and on behalf
               of, a licensee. Alcohol means the product of distillation of any fermented liquid, whether rectified or diluted,
               whatever may be the origin thereof, and includes synthetic ethyl alcohol. The term
               "alcohol" does not include denatured alcohol or wood alcohol.…

               99-46, shall be deemed the official comprehensive plan and may be amended from time
               to time in accordance with section 11-12-7 of the Illinois municipal code, 65 Illinois
               Compiled Statutes 5/11-12-7. B. Jurisdiction: The official comprehensive plan shall encompass all of the land within
               the municipality and within one and one-half (1½) miles of the boundaries of the municipality,
               insofar as the same are not included in any city, Village or incorporated town. C. Definition: The "official comprehensive plan" shall be defined as a compilation of
               policy statements; goals; standards; maps; recommended planning, regulatory, fiscal
               and public works programs; and any other matter relative to the present and future
               patterns of life within the jurisdictional area stated in subsection B of this section,
               and shall include, but is not limited to, the following elements which are in general
               conformance with the state of Illinois planning and technical assistance act (public
               act 92-0768): 1. Issues and Opportunities: A statement of the vision of the community, identification

questions.prompt: Which trees in a required yard on a private Northbrook lot are protected?
choices: Any tree that will reach 8 feet tall

questions.answer: Trees 6 inches or more in diameter measured 4.5 feet above the ground
questions.excerpt:
The regulation of trees by this Code is intended to accomplish the protection, preservation,
               replacement, planting and maintenance of trees within the village and the following
               related goals: (1) Stabilize valuable topsoil by preventing or minimizing unnecessary soil erosion and
                  sedimentation; (2) Assist in controlling proper storm water runoff in order to decrease the costs associated
                  with flooding; protect the important link in the hydrologic cycle that trees provide
                  through the transpiring of water and the neutralization of wastes that pass through
                  to the groundwater table and other aquifers; (3) Aid in the reduction of air pollution through the removal of harmful carbon dioxide,
                  the generation of oxygen, and the precipitation of dust and other airborne pollutants; (4) Provide a buffer and screen against noise pollution; (5) Restore to the greatest extent possible denuded soil that results from construction
                  and grading work accompanying development; (6) Provide a haven and nesting areas for birds, insects, and other forms of wildlife
                  that are essential to the maintenance of the food chain and that help control and
                  eliminate disease-carrying mosquitoes; (7) Reduce energy consumption through the wind break and shade, effects of trees; (8) Protect and increase property values in a manner that maintains each property owner's
                  enjoyment of their property; (9) Conserve and enhance the village's physical and aesthetic environment; (10) Eliminate trees that constitute a threat, danger, or nuisance to the public or to
                  property in the village, or that may be dangerous to the health of other trees and
                  vegetation in the village; (11) Encourage coordination between property owners and village officials to allow for
                  the coexistence of…

questions.prompt: In Poplar Grove, it is a violation to park a vehicle in areas marked by which of these?
choices: "No Parking" signs or painted yellow lines on the curb
questions.answer: "No Parking" signs or painted yellow lines on the curb
questions.excerpt:
A. No Parking Areas. It shall be a violation of this section to park a vehicle in areas
               marked by "No Parking" signs or marked by painted yellow lines on the curb. B. Parking Against Traffic Flow. It shall be a violation of this section to park a vehicle
               against the flow of traffic on the side of the street heading into the flow of traffic. C. Obstructing Traffic. No person shall park or place any vehicles or other property
               within the streets or highways of the Village so as to obstruct or interfere with
               traffic or travel or other vehicles or pedestrians or endanger public safety. D. Semitruck and Trailer Parking. It shall be unlawful for the operator or owner of any
               motor vehicle except a passenger vehicle, public utility truck, and trucks licensed
               by the state under the classification of A or B license, to park such vehicles within
               residential areas in the Village for a period of longer than one hour. If a tractor-trailer or unattached trailer is parked completely off residential streets
               and sidewalks in private driveways on the driver's property and not obstructing view
               to prevent a safety hazard, then it shall be considered exempt from this subsection. E. Weight Limits. No vehicle or combination of vehicles, unladen or with load shall be
               driven on streets within the Village posted "NO TRUCKS" when said vehicle carries
               an Illinois license designation greater than B or equivalent, or its equivalent out
               of state license. The requirements of this subsection shall not apply to commercial vehicles parked
               within the Village limits for the purpose of collecting or delivering persons, materials
               or merchandise or performing some service to the residents on whose property or adjacent
               property the vehicle is being parked. F. Unattended Vehicles Parked…

               liquors shall be fostered and promoted. (Code 1996, § 5.15.010)

               meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates
               a different meaning: Alcohol means the product of distillation of any fermented liquid, whether rectified or diluted,
               whatever may be the origin thereof, and includes synthetic ethyl alcohol. It does

               or beer and capable of being consumed by a person. The provisions of this chapter
               shall not apply to alcohol used in the manufacture of denatured alcohol produced in
               accordance with Acts of Congress and regulations promulgated thereunder, nor to any
               liquid or solid containing one-half of one percent or less of alcohol, by volume.

The village has adopted by reference, as a part of this chapter, the Illinois Vehicle
               Code, 625 ILCS 5/1-100 et seq., except those administrative provisions which by their
               nature cannot apply to the village. The references in that code to its provisions
               generally shall apply to this chapter. (Prior Code, § 8-3; Code 2007, § 70.02)

Members of the police department and special police assigned to traffic duty are authorized
               to direct, control, and regulate all traffic in accordance with the provisions of
               this chapter, or in emergencies, as public safety or convenience may require. Except
               in case of emergency, it is unlawful for any person not authorized by law or this
               Code to direct or attempt to direct traffic. (Prior Code, § 8-6; Code 2007, § 70.03)

(a) The provisions of this chapter regulating the movement and parking of vehicles shall
               not apply to the driver of any authorized emergency vehicle when responding to an
               emergency call, but the driver upon approaching a red or stop signal or stop sign
               shall reduce the speed of the vehicle as necessary for safety but may proceed cautiously
               past a red or stop signal or stop sign. At other times, drivers of authorized vehicles
               shall stop in obedience to a stop sign or signal. (b) No driver of any authorized emergency vehicle shall assume any special privileges
               under this chapter, except when the vehicle is operated in response to an emergency

questions.excerpt:
Footnotes: --- ( 1 ) --- Editor's note— Ord. No. 2303-93, § 1, adopted Mar. 8, 1993, repealed former ch. 3, §§ 3-1—3-30, 3-51—3-66,
               which pertained to similar subject matter, in its entirety, and enacted a new ch.
               3 to read as herein set out. See the Code Comparative Table for a detailed analysis
               of inclusion. Cross reference— Discontinuance of sale of alcoholic liquor during emergency, § 2-327(2), (3); licenses generally, Ch. 9; public intoxication, § 13-8.

The provisions of this chapter may be cited and referred to as the "Roselle Liquor
               Control Ordinance." (Ord. No. 2303-93, § 1, 3-8-93)

It is the policy of the Village of Roselle (hereinafter "village") to limit and control
               the retail sale of alcoholic liquor so as not to require the tax payer to directly
               or indirectly subsidize: liquor sales; the regulation of liquor sales; or police activities
               necessary to control liquor sales. Further, it is the policy of the village to limit
               the purchase, consumption or possession of alcoholic liquor by persons under twenty-one
               (21) years of age, incompetents, and intoxicated persons and further to prevent public
               intoxication, disorderly conduct, traffic accidents, unruly disturbances at public
               or private assemblies, driving while intoxicated and similar conduct which can result
               from the sale and excessive consumption of alcoholic liquor and to promote temperance
               in the consumption of alcoholic liquor. The remaining provisions of this chapter shall
               be interpreted to further these purposes. (Ord. No. 2303-93, § 1, 3-8-93)

               whatever may be the origin thereof including synthetic ethyl alcohol. This definition

questions.prompt: In Springfield, can you take glass, paper, aluminum cans, or a recycling bin from someone else's property?
choices: Yes, if they left it at the curb
No, not without the owner's prior written permission
Yes, as long as you leave the container
questions.answer: No, not without the owner's prior written permission
questions.excerpt:
(a) Any person who enters upon the land or any part thereof of another, after receiving,
               immediately prior to the entry, notice from the owner or occupant that an entry is
               forbidden, or remains upon the land of another after receiving notice from the owner
               or occupant to depart, commits the offense of trespass to land. (b) A person has received notice from the owner or occupant within the meaning of subsection
               (a) if he has been notified personally, either orally or in writing, or if a printed
               or written notice forbidding entry has been conspicuously posted or exhibited at the
               main entrance to the land or the forbidden part thereof.

(a) For the purposes of this section, "property" means anything of value, including, but
               not limited to, real estate, money, commercial instruments, written instruments representing
               or embodying rights concerning anything of value, labor, or services, things affixed

questions.excerpt:
Chapters:

Sections:

The construction, maintenance and repair of public streets, alleys, sidewalks and
               other dedicated public ways under the jurisdiction of the village of Westchester or
               the installation therein or thereon of any improvements including, but not limited
               to, street lights, water mains, sewer and gas, telephone or electric services, shall
               be under the supervision of the public works superintendent. He shall be charged with
               the enforcement of all ordinance provisions relating to such public places or public
               improvements (except traffic ordinances) and is authorized to enforce such ordinances. (Ord. No. 2010-1842, § 4, 2-9-2010; Ord. 62-651 § 1, 1962)

It is unlawful to construct or lay any pavement on any public street, sidewalk, alley
               or other dedicated public way under the jurisdiction of the village of Westchester,
               or to repair the same or to engage in any of the work contemplated by Section 12.04.010 whether the same is let under a private or public contract, without having first
               secured a permit therefor. Applications for such permits shall be made to the public
               works superintendent and shall state the location of the intended pavement or repair,
               the extent thereof, and the person or firm who is to do the actual construction work.

               of the village. (Ord. No. 2010-1842, § 4, 2-9-2010; Ord. 62-651 § 2, 1962)

questions.excerpt:
The provisions of this chapter may be cited and referred to as the "Wheaton Liquor
               Control Ordinance." (Code 1968, § 3-1; Code 1996, § 6-1)

It is the policy of the city to limit the sale of alcoholic liquor at retail primarily
               to the sale in its original package, or by restaurants, recreational facilities or
               hotels as defined in this chapter. It is not deemed conducive to the promotion of
               this public policy to allow the sale of alcoholic liquor at retail for the consumption
               on the premises where such sale is the sole or primary business to be conducted. Further,
               it is the policy of the city to limit the purchase, consumption, or possession of
               alcoholic liquor to persons of the age of 21 years or older in order to prevent intoxication,
               disorderly conduct, trespasses, unruly disturbances at public or private assemblies,
               traffic accidents, and similar conduct which often results from the purchase, consumption,
               or possession of alcoholic liquor by persons under the lawful age. (Code 1968, § 3-2; Code 1996, § 6-2)

The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the
               meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates
               a different meaning: Alcoholic liquor means any spirits, wine, beer, ale, or other liquid containing more than one-half
               of one percent of alcohol by volume, which is fit for beverage purposes. Beverages
               sold as beer, ale, or other designation commonly applied to malt beverages containing
               more than one-half of one percent of alcohol by volume shall be presumed to be alcoholic
               liquor for the purposes of this chapter. Bar means any counter at which alcoholic beverages may be stored, displayed, prepared
               or served and at which patrons are permitted…

questions.excerpt:
The following provisions of article I shall apply only in the unincorporated area
               of the county. (Compiled Ords. 2013, § 4-1; Amend. of 6-17-2014, § 4.0)

The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the
               meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates
               a different meaning: Alcohol means the product of distillation of any fermented liquid, whether rectified or diluted,
               whatever may be the origin thereof, and includes synthetic ethyl alcohol. It does
               not include denatured alcohol or wood alcohol. Alcoholic liquor includes alcohol, spirits, wine and beer, and every liquid or solid, patented or
               not, containing alcohol, spirits, wine or beer, and capable of being consumed as a
               beverage by a human being. Beer means a beverage obtained by the alcoholic fermentation of an infusion or concoction
               of barley, or other grain, malt and hops in water, and includes, among other things,
               beer, ale, stout, lager beer, porter and the like. Building means any structure having a roof supported by columns or walls and intended for
               shelter, housing or enclosure of any individual, process, equipment, goods or materials
               of any kind or nature. Building shall include an outside area which is directly accessible
               from and adjacent to the building so long as the outside area has an enclosure of
               at least six feet in height, and is no more than 3,000 square feet in area. All fences
               shall be constructed of ornamental iron, wood, stone or picket, shall be maintained
               in good repair and shall be painted or treated in such other fashion so as to maintain
               a neat appearance at all times. Wooden posts shall be treated with a wood preserver
               before being placed underground. All portions…
